stage_pressure_definition: p = lam*max_k c_k + (1-lam)*sum_k c_k/4 over urgency/scarcity/social_proof/misdirection, c_k = max calibrated P(dark) of flagged findings of category k; lam = 0.5 (backend/intelligence/pressure.py)
caveats: No ground truth exists for journey pressure, choice asymmetry or composite deception; nothing here is real-world validation.
A1 and A3 are pure mathematics of the weighting schemes; A3 confirms the score is linear in each stage pressure (marginal = 100*w_i).
A2 and A4 journeys are SYNTHETIC: random combinations of real held-out TEST-split strings. A4 labels come from the construction.

B choice sets and screenshots are SYNTHETIC and AUTHORED (markup, CSS, accept labels, 'No thanks', headings); levels come from the construction. Decline wordings marked misdirection_test_split are verbatim TEST-split rows.
B uses hex colours on purpose; see the bug note about rgb()/rgba() backgrounds written with spaces (mcai.html_visual_features).
C describes the shipped demo inputs; demo journeys are themselves synthetic and flagged as such.
D is circular: the same classifier scores originals and rewrites, so it measures removal of model cues, not consumer impact.
Stage pressures use the text threshold (clf.b.threshold); below-threshold elements contribute 0 by design (pressure.py).
All Fibonacci/linear/equal weights and CDI/MCAI weights are design choices (backend/intelligence/config.py), not learned.

The classifier scores the neutral decline 'No thanks' as misdirection (see D.neutral_decline_score): every dataset row starting 'No thanks' is labelled misdirection. This inflates the MCAI semantic 'guilt' sub-score for neutral declines (B) and keeps counterfactual misdirection rewrites above threshold (D).

The classifier also flags neutral stock/deadline statements (e.g. '1 in stock.'), i.e. it scores the content, not only the pressure wording; scarcity rewrites therefore rarely fall below threshold (D).

A2_order_sensitivity.design: 500 synthetic 4-stage journeys; each stage = 3 distinct TEST-split strings drawn uniformly at random (any label) and joined with newlines; stage pressure = content_pressure(Auditor.audit(segment_text(stage),'text').findings), i.e. exactly the per-stage quantity the engine uses for a text stage. Positions 1..4 (submission order). Escalating = the journey's 4 pressures sorted ascending; de-escalating = sorted descending.
A2_order_sensitivity.note: Equal weighting is order-invariant by construction (every permutation gives the same score); the measured max |difference| for 'equal' is floating-point noise only. Ties for fibonacci/linear occur only when all four stage pressures are identical.

A3_single_stage_perturbation.design: Same 500 sampled journeys as A2. For position i, set p_i=0 and p_i=1 (others at their sampled values); marginal = score(p_i=1) - score(p_i=0). Theory: marginal = 100 * w_i exactly.

A4_synthetic_discrimination.kind: synthetic labelled benchmark - measures whether the weighting behaves as designed, NOT real-world validity
A4_synthetic_discrimination.design: 300 synthetic 4-stage journeys (100 per group). Every stage has 3 real TEST-split strings. 'late': stages 3-4 each contain 1 random dark (label != benign) string + 2 benign strings, stages 1-2 are 3 benign strings; 'early': the mirror image; 'none': benign strings only. Labels come from this construction. Stage pressure as in A2. Benign strings can be false positives of the classifier and dark strings can be missed, so 'none' is not 0 by construction.
A4_synthetic_discrimination.bootstrap: 95% percentile CI over 1000 bootstrap resamples of each group (seeded).

legacy_noisy_or_comparison_submission_or.note: Same journeys, stage pressure = noisy-OR of the same category maxima (the pre-change definition). Comparison only.

B_mcai_synthetic_html.kind: synthetic labelled benchmark (designed asymmetry level = number of visual asymmetry factors applied)
B_mcai_synthetic_html.design: All subsets of size 0..5 of 6 visual asymmetry factors {weight: accept 700 vs decline 400; size: 20px vs 13px; fill: accept filled #0f766e/white text vs decline transparent; link: decline is an <a> text link instead of a <button>; grey: decline text #b0b0b0 (low contrast) instead of #111111; opacity: decline opacity 0.55} = 63 designs, each with two decline wordings: the AUTHORED neutral 'No thanks' and a random TEST-split misdirection row that the decline lexicon recognises. Accept label (AUTHORED) is constant. Declared HTML/CSS only (hex colours). Interaction dimension is unavailable (no declared step counts), so MCAI = visual (w 0.4) + semantic (w 0.3), renormalised.

B_mcai_synthetic_screenshots.match_rule: an option counts as found if the OCR text matches the rendered text with difflib ratio >= 0.85 after lower-casing and removing non-alphanumerics; exact_ocr_text reports exact matches

D_counterfactual_rewrites.circularity_caveat: The same classifier that flagged the original scores the rewrite, so a drop in P(dark) shows that the rewrite removes the cues the model relies on - not that consumers would be less pressured, and not independent validation of the redesign.
